title: Rig event envelope
description: What a rig sends back. The canonical spec: event.js validates against it in JavaScript, the ingest service generates its Pydantic models from it, and fixtures/ is what proves the two still agree. Every field outside `data` comes from the schedule the desk pushed, which is what makes the payload the dimension table for the whole event stream.

eventId.description: Minted on the rig at pedal-press, before anything downstream is told. Ingest dedupes on (rigId, eventId), which is what lets the uploader retry blindly forever.

seq.description: Per-rig and monotonic. max(seq) is the uploader's cursor: on reconnect the rig asks what the server holds and resends only what follows.

at.description: Wall clock on the rig, ISO 8601 with a zone. The server stores received_at alongside it, so clock skew is measurable for free.

shiftDate.description: From the pushed payload's shift.date, not from the rig's own clock.

turnFrom.description: Start of the turn in progress. Null when nothing is scheduled - a rig on standby still reports a shift check.

operatorId.description: The operator the schedule places at this rig for this turn. Null on standby. The rig never asks anyone who they are; this comes from the payload.

operatorName.description: The name of the person in that seat, as the pushed payload named them. operatorId is a seat rather than a person - rotation-engine builds it as "op-" + group + slot, so the same id is a different human on a cover day - and no other table keeps a name. Optional, never required: events queued before the field existed have none, and a rig discards a refused batch rather than retrying it.

bucket.description: The table this row lands in on the far side.

data.description: Bucket-specific measurements. Never a conclusion: no percentages, no formatted durations, no prose. A stored ratio cannot be corrected without re-running the floor; the numbers it was made of can.
The four seconds columns, and no efficiency figure. Efficiency is recordedSecs / (assignedSecs - faultSecs - downSecs), computed at read time from one definition.

chargedTo.description: The app already draws this distinction on the wall - 'found at handover, charged to the previous operator'. It is a fact about a person's shift, so it has to survive into the data.
